memory_update.text: GEV is the clearest direct equipment bottleneck candidate for dispatchable gas generation because public filings show rapidly expanding gas turbine backlog/slot reservations and data-center-related electrification orders.

BKR should be tracked as a second-order but direct equipment supplier: LNG compression, aeroderivative gas turbines, BRUSH generators, power-generation equipment, monitoring, and aftermarket services.
LNG is the cleanest US-listed LNG export asset-owner candidate for the LNG ramp component of this node; main diligence is train completion, FERC/DOE approvals, feedgas basis, and contract coverage.

WMB and ET are both high-relevance pipeline/gas-delivery candidates for the data-center power chokepoint; ET currently shows more explicit named data-center/utility gas-contract disclosures, while WMB shows behind-the-meter project framing.

ETR was not included in the five-candidate cap but deserves a follow-up pass under regulated utilities/IPPs with permitted gas projects because of Meta/Richland Parish gas-generation and transmission approvals.

GEV is the highest-confidence direct equipment candidate for the gas turbine and grid-equipment bottleneck; next pass should check backlog quality, production expansion, and OEM competitive landscape versus Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy, which are not primary US-listed common stocks.

BKR should remain in the universe as an LNG and gas-infrastructure equipment supplier; inclusion depends on evidence that compression/turbomachinery procurement is capacity constrained and material to backlog.
WMB is a strong midstream candidate because it has a disclosed data-center pipeline-capacity agreement; track whether additional gas-to-data-center contracts enter backlog.

The node appears to be a deliverability stack rather than a single commodity trade: turbine slots, LNG export ramp, pipeline capacity, gas basis, utility regulatory approvals, and transmission all interact.

Potential omitted candidates for later expansion include Energy Transfer, Kinder Morgan, TC Energy, Fluor, KBR, Chart Industries, Venture Global, Vistra, NRG, and Bloom Energy; they were excluded here only due to the five-candidate limit.

GEV remains the primary direct gas-turbine chokepoint candidate; future passes should separate heavy-duty turbines, aeroderivative bridge-power turbines, turbine services, and grid/electrification exposure.
BKR should be tracked as an LNG/gas-infrastructure equipment supplier rather than a pure oilfield-services proxy; key evidence is LNG turbomachinery order flow and IET backlog.
ET maps to regional deliverability and basis constraints; Desert Southwest and Louisiana-related gas-transport agreements are more relevant to the node than generic commodity gas exposure.

ETR is a regulated-asset/data-center-load case: upside logic depends on approved rate-base growth and customer-funded infrastructure, while falsification risk is regulatory disallowance or backlash over cost allocation.

POWL is a less obvious adjacent chokepoint candidate because LNG terminals, pipelines, gas plants, and utility interconnects require engineered electrical distribution and switchgear; verify whether backlog directly contains LNG/gas-power/data-center projects.

Not yet expanded: Cheniere/NextDecade/Venture Global LNG exporters, Williams/Kinder Morgan/DT Midstream pipeline operators, EPC firms such as Fluor/KBR/Primoris, and controls/components suppliers such as Woodward; these require a separate pass to avoid overloading this layer.

node: Dispatchable gas generation, gas turbines, pipelines, and LNG
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded universe for the dispatchable gas power/LNG node. The strongest direct exposures found in this pass are: gas-turbine and electrification OEM GE Vernova; LNG and gas-power turbomachinery supplier Baker Hughes; LNG export asset owner Cheniere; pipeline/behind-the-meter gas-power platform Williams; and pipeline/storage platform Energy Transfer. All five appear above the USD 1B market-cap preference based on current market-data snapshot, but this pass is research support only and does not imply a buy/sell view. Expanded universe for the dispatchable gas power / LNG chokepoint. The strongest public-market mappings are gas-turbine OEM capacity, LNG compression and power-generation equipment, gas pipeline deliverability into data-center and power-load clusters, LNG export capacity ramp timing, and regulated utilities with large gas-generation buildouts. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded universe for the dispatchable-gas-power/LNG node. The clearest chokepoint mapping is not simply upstream gas production, but scarce deliverable capacity: heavy-duty and aeroderivative gas turbines, LNG and gas-compression equipment, pipeline expansions into constrained load pockets, regulated utility generation/transmission buildouts, and electrical distribution gear used in LNG, pipeline, power-generation, and utility projects. Candidates below are research leads only, not recommendations.
